body.heading: Small enough to survive busy days
paragraphs: Full-page journaling is lovely and, for most people, unsustainable. Three sentences is the minimum viable diary: one about what happened, one about how it felt, one about anything at all.
That tiny record turns out to be surprisingly rich. Months later, three honest sentences bring a day back more vividly than a calendar full of appointments ever will.

body.heading: Attach it to an existing moment
paragraphs: Write your three sentences at the same point each day — in bed before sleep works well, or with morning tea. Anchoring the habit to an existing moment means you rarely have to remember it deliberately.
Missed a day? Write three sentences about yesterday, or simply start again today. A record with gaps is still a record; a perfect streak abandoned in week two is not.

takeaway: One event, one feeling, one anything: three sentences is a diary that lasts.
